Hi Mike and Support Team,

I am writing to file an official RMA claim for my NerdQaxe++ Rev 6.1 from Order Shop···· (Delivered April 22).
To be completely frank, I am beyond frustrated. I have had an endless amount of trouble and nonsense with HeliumDeploy as a company. I’ve tried to be a patient and loyal customer, but receiving yet another defective product that dies after short, normal usage is the final straw. Last time I had a hardware issue with you, it took a ridiculous 5 months of constant chasing on my end to get a replacement, which cost me lost earnings. I will not accept a repeat of that circus. I expect this to be handled ASAP and without the endless stalling, delays, and poor follow-up I have been subjected to in the past.

According to your own RMA policy, power delivery issues and hashboard failures on the NerdQaxe++ are explicitly covered under warranty.

### Technical Details & Diagnosis:

* **Error Message:** The onboard screen displays: **`VOLTAGE PROTECTION - Guru Meditation #····`**.

* **Power Input:** The web dashboard confirms an active input voltage of **12.3 V** from the power supply.

* **ASIC/VRM Output:** The internal voltage regulator fails to pass voltage to the ASIC chips, showing **`Current ASIC Voltage: 0.00 V`**, **`Current Input: 0.00 A`**, and **` Power Usage: 0.1 W`**.

* **Settings:** All settings are at default (`Frequency: 600 MHz`, `Core Voltage: 1150 mV`).

### RMA Request:

Per your RMA program guidelines:

1. Please email me the **prepaid return label** for your European hub.

2. As this unit has failed, please issue a replacement or process a refund upon receipt.

I have attached screenshots showing the screen error and the web interface with the 0.00 V ASIC reading.

--
Mvh / regards
Raymond H.
Note to the team: I'll pull up the order and the RMA state before I reply.

Thank you for the quick, straightforward reply and for acknowledging the previous issues. I appreciate you handling this directly.

I would like to go with the Hammer replacement (Hammer Miner Thor P2 10 TH/s). Please set this unit aside for my RMA.

Looking forward to getting the label and tracking for the replacement unit.

---
Mvh / regards
Raymond H.

If any step stops, flag it and tell them the team will confirm the next step by email.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
